rows.name: get_context
rows.summary: A high-quality definition: clear purpose, explicit sibling alternatives, and topic-level constraints and return shapes. Only minor cost is length.

rows.name: list_entities
rows.summary: Excellent definition that compensates for a large schema with clear per-type rules and explicit return shapes. Length is the only tradeoff.

rows.name: search_transactions
rows.summary: Strong, mode-based definition that ties parameters to variants and spells out return shapes. Dense but appropriately so.

rows.name: summarize_transactions
rows.summary: Well-structured report selector with explicit sibling alternatives, per-report parameter rules, and documented returns. Strong across the board.

rows.name: list_budget_months
rows.summary: A tight, complete definition for a small tool. Good sibling routing and return documentation; transparency slightly less rich because annotations already carry the safety story.

rows.name: run_query
rows.summary: Outstanding definition for a complex tool: full grammar, refusal behavior, table inventory, and return hints. Length is warranted by the surface.

rows.name: manage_transactions
rows.summary: Comprehensive multi-action write tool with explicit destructive warnings and per-action returns. Only slight gap is mode-choice guidance between update variants.

rows.name: manage_accounts
rows.summary: Detailed, well-routed write tool with strong disclosure of destructive and side-effecting behavior. Minor density in the update clause.

rows.name: manage_categories
rows.summary: Clear, consequence-aware write tool with good sibling routing and documented returns. One of the cleaner manage definitions.

rows.name: manage_payees
rows.summary: Well-written write tool that warns about transfer-payee refusals and merge consequences, with per-action returns. Consistently strong.

rows.name: manage_tags
rows.summary: A strong, dense definition: purpose and write/read split are explicit, destructive behavior is described in detail, and per-action return shapes compensate for the missing output schema. Only the paragraph formatting slightly hurts scanability.

rows.name: manage_rules
rows.summary: An exemplary definition for a complex tool: it documents atomicity gaps, idempotency behavior of upsert, operator/field constraints, and return shapes that annotations and schema omit. Length is justified, though formatting could be improved.

rows.name: manage_schedules
rows.summary: Highly informative: the destructive delete side effects, recurrence/amount_op coupling, and unsettable fields are all disclosed. Purpose and alternatives are explicit, so an agent can select and invoke it confidently.

rows.name: manage_budget_months
rows.summary: Behaviorally excellent, with atomicity, clamping, and buffer-additive risks clearly disclosed. The main weakness is structure: a single sprawling paragraph for seven actions is hard to parse, though content-wise it is thorough.

rows.name: manage_budget_files
rows.summary: A strong, safety-forward definition: the surprising session-active-budget change on import and the local-copy replacement are clearly disclosed, alongside output shapes. Some parameter detail duplicates the schema, but the behavioral warnings justify the length.
